data.narrative:
Electra is a Series B climate and energy company founded by Sandeep Nijhawan and Quoc Pham that has raised $299M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comparable universe of 9 private frontier-tech companies in climate and energy (including KoBold Metals, Electric Hydrogen, and Amogy at Series C stage) and 1 public comparable (Linz Energy, ticker LNZA).

Two triangulation methods are applicable. Stage-progression analysis applies a 1.9x step-up multiplier typical of Series B-to-next-stage advancement to the $299M raised proxy, implying a valuation of $568M. Peer-median analysis across the three same-sector, adjacent-stage comparables yields a median valuation of $1.0B, with a range spanning $700M (Amogy) to $3.0B (KoBold Metals). The peer-median method reflects Electra's positioning within a competitive set of later-stage capital raises in the climate technology space.

Triangulating these two methods produces a valuation range of $483M (low) to $1.1B (high), with a median of $784M. The $301M spread between stage-progression and peer-median reflects uncertainty around comparable company selection and stage-normalization. Key sensitivities include: (1) capital efficiency relative to peer cohort; (2) timing and terms of the next financing event; and (3) technology and commercialization risk within the frontier-energy sector, where peer valuations span a three-fold range.
